history.period: 1950s or earlier (UNVERIFIED — reported 'more than 70 years' old in 2024); current structure inaugurated August 1993
history.summary: Historic Hindu temple inside an Assam Rifles complex in central Aizawl — business listings place it at Khatla 796001, while a 2024 report locates the Hari Mandir at Canteen Square (previously in the AR complex at Bethlehem); locality needs verification. Maintained by Assam Rifles, it is the religious and cultural centre for Aizawl's Gorkha Hindus and Bru Reangs, hosting Durga Puja, Diwali, Janmashtami, weddings and kirtans. On 23 May 2013 a gelatin-bomb explosion shattered 26 window panes of the temple inside the 26th Battalion Assam Rifles compound, on the day of an MNF 'anti-idol-worshipping' rally. A plaque notes the shrine was destroyed by miscreants and reconstructed by Brigadier Shri Ram Singh, inaugurated by the Commandant of 1st Battalion Assam Rifles in August 1993. In September 2024 the Mizoram Gorkha Mandir Sanchalan Samiti petitioned the 2nd Assam Rifles Commandant to keep the temple's administration with the local Hindu community amid fears it would pass to the state government when AR bases relocate from Aizawl to Zokhawsang. Media image is the actual temple gate (reads 'Hari Mandir Assam Rifles'), verified visually. Coordinates are for the geocoded 'Assam Rifles Mandir' (Bungkawn Vengthar) and are approximate.

name: Assam Rifles Mandir (Hari Mandir)
town_description: Aizawl is the capital of Mizoram, a hill city built on steep ridges at around 1,130 m elevation in the state's northern hills. Overwhelmingly Christian (Mizo) in population, it is the political, commercial and cultural centre of the state. The Assam Rifles — the paramilitary 'Sentinels of the North East' — has had major bases in the heart of Aizawl (Zodin, Khatla, Canteen Square) since colonial times, and its Hindu troops founded the mandirs that anchor the city's small Gorkha Hindu community.
